Days 1–2
Islands
Days 1–2
Nosy Be

Arrival & Lokobe Forest

Welcome to Madagascar. You'll be met at Nosy Be Airport and transferred to a rustic beachfront camp nestled near the edge of Lokobe Forest Reserve — one of Madagascar's last remaining lowland rainforests. Spend the remainder of Day 1 relaxing, taking in your first impressions of the island, and enjoying dinner under the stars with the sounds of the forest and sea around you.

Beachfront camp accommodationFirst impressions of Nosy Be
Camp is accessible by short boat transfer from the mainland.
Day 2
Wildlife
Day 2
Ankarana Special Reserve

Journey to Ankarana

After breakfast on the beach, depart by fast boat to Ankify on Madagascar's mainland. From Ankify, continue north on a scenic overland journey through the dry forests of the north to the remarkable Ankarana Special Reserve — a spectacular limestone massif featuring underground rivers, caves and the razor-sharp tsingy formations that are among Madagascar's most extraordinary natural landscapes. After checking into your lodge, enjoy the afternoon to explore at your own pace before the optional guided night walk, where you may encounter some of the reserve's fascinating nocturnal species including tenrecs, chameleons and sleeping lemurs.

Fast boat transfer to AnkifyScenic overland drive northAnkarana limestone tsingy formationsOptional guided night walk
The overland journey from Ankify to Ankarana takes approximately 2–3 hours. Good walking shoes recommended for the tsingy terrain.
Day 3
Adventure
Day 3
Ankarana → Diego Suarez

Tsingy & the Road to Diego

Spend the morning exploring the extraordinary tsingy landscapes of Ankarana. The sharp limestone pinnacles, deep canyons and dry forest corridors are home to lemurs, endemic birds and rare plant species found nowhere else on earth. A variety of guided trails are available, ranging from easy walks to more adventurous cave explorations. After lunch, continue north to Diego Suarez — Antsiranana — a vibrant coastal town known for its spectacular natural harbour and colourful blend of Malagasy culture and French colonial heritage. From Diego, transfer south to Sakalava Bay, your base for the next few nights.

Morning tsingy explorationGuided trails: easy walks to cave adventuresDrive through northern MadagascarArrival at Sakalava Bay
Diego Suarez is approximately 1.5 hours north of Ankarana. Sakalava Bay is a short transfer south of the town.
Days 3–6
Relax
Days 3–6
Sakalava Bay

Leisurely Days on the Bay

Sakalava Bay is a beautiful, unhurried stretch of coastline renowned for its crystal-clear waters, white sandy beaches and a steady ocean breeze that makes it one of the best kitesurfing spots in northern Madagascar. Days here are genuinely at leisure — swim, rest, explore the coastline or try kitesurfing with local instructors. In the evenings, savour exceptionally fresh seafood and watch the sun descend over the Indian Ocean from the terrace of your beachfront accommodation.

Kitesurfing (equipment & instructors available)Swimming and beach walksFresh seafood dinnersSnorkelling off the bay
Sakalava Bay is best known for kitesurfing between May and November when the trade winds are strongest.
Days 6–9
Marine
Days 6–9
Emerald Sea (Mer d'Émeraude)

The Emerald Sea

Depart Sakalava Bay for a short transfer to one of northern Madagascar's most breathtaking natural wonders — the Emerald Sea. This extraordinary turquoise lagoon is protected by a coral reef and fringed by pristine white sandbanks, creating conditions of almost impossible clarity and colour. Accessible by traditional sailboat, the area is ideal for snorkelling in the shallow, warm waters, discovering secluded islets by pirogue, or simply lying on untouched beaches with nothing but birdsong for company. Your seaside accommodation here is a simple, beautiful base from which to explore fully at your own pace.

Traditional sailboat to the lagoonWorld-class snorkelling in the reefSecluded islet exploration by pirogueComplete serenity — very few other visitors
The Emerald Sea is accessible by boat from the Diego Suarez area. The lagoon is best explored early morning when the light is extraordinary.
Days 9–11
Islands
Days 9–11
Return to Nosy Be

Back to the Islands

After breakfast, begin your journey back south to Nosy Be via Ankify. Upon arrival, transfer to your beachfront hotel on the west coast of the island, overlooking the beautiful turquoise waters surrounding Sakatia Island. The hotel combines Malagasy charm with modern comfort — ocean-view rooms, tropical gardens and inviting swimming pools make for a very welcome return to island life. Spend your evening at leisure, perhaps enjoying a sunset cocktail on the beach as you settle back into the Nosy Be rhythm.

Overland journey back via AnkifyBeachfront hotel — Sakatia Island viewsSunset from the west coast beachOptional Nosy Be Island Tour
The return journey from Diego Suarez to Nosy Be via Ankify takes a full day. An early start is recommended.
Days 11–12
Marine
Days 11–12
Nosy Iranja & Whale Shark Excursion

Whale Sharks & Turtle Island

Depart early for an unforgettable whale shark excursion — available seasonally from October to December — where you will snorkel alongside the largest fish in the ocean in their natural environment. Guided by experienced marine specialists, this responsible, eco-conscious experience is one of the most remarkable wildlife encounters anywhere in the Indian Ocean. After the excursion, continue to the breathtaking island of Nosy Iranja, often called Turtle Island, famous for its dazzling white sandbar connecting two islands at low tide. Spend the afternoon swimming, snorkelling in the crystal lagoon or relaxing on pristine beaches under palm trees. A freshly prepared seafood lunch is served in the shade. In the evening, settle into your rustic beachfront villa and during nesting season you may witness sea turtles coming ashore under the stars.

Whale shark excursion (Oct–Dec, seasonal)Nosy Iranja iconic twin-island sandbarHawksbill sea turtle nesting (seasonal)Overnight in beachfront villa
The whale shark excursion runs October to December only. Outside this period, the Nosy Iranja day is a full marine experience in its own right.
Days 12–14
Wildlife
Days 12–14
Nosy Komba

The Lemur Island

Transfer from Nosy Iranja to the lush volcanic island of Nosy Komba — the Island of Lemurs. Your accommodation here offers an intimate eco-luxury experience focused on sustainability, comfort and authentic island hospitality. Beautifully designed bungalows overlook the sea, while the lodge's signature restaurant serves fresh cuisine inspired by local Malagasy flavours. During your stay, enjoy guided forest walks where black lemurs approach freely, kayaking in the calm waters, paddleboarding, snorkelling off the island's fringing reef and visits to nearby fishing villages where you can learn about traditional Malagasy life and culture.

Semi-wild black lemur encountersEco-luxury bungalow accommodationKayaking & paddleboardingTraditional village visitsGuided snorkelling from shore
Nosy Komba is a 20-minute boat transfer from Nosy Iranja. No vehicles on the island — all exploration is on foot or by water.
Day 14
Departure
Day 14
Departure

Farewell to Madagascar

After a final breakfast overlooking the ocean, enjoy a scenic boat transfer back to Nosy Be for your onward flight. As you cross the turquoise channel between Nosy Komba and the mainland, take in the final views of Madagascar's remarkable islands — the green volcanic peaks, the pirogues drifting at anchor and the extraordinary quality of light that you will not find anywhere else on earth. Madagascar has a habit of staying with you long after you leave.

Scenic morning boat transferFinal views of the Nosy Be archipelagoTransfer to Nosy Be Airport
Allow sufficient time for the boat transfer and airport check-in. Early departures can be arranged with advance notice.
